subject: Clarifying scope for upcoming vulnerability assessment across hosting variants
messages:
From: Blue Harbor Security <sec+bh@blueharbor.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming vulnerability assessment — scope confirmation

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for coordinating. We're the third-party team conducting the vulnerability assessment for Acme Corp's Redwood integration. Before we finalize the test plan we need to confirm which components Redwood is asking us to include under the assessment. In particular: 

- Hosted (Redwood-managed): control plane, runtime nodes in Redwood regions, admin consoles, logging/telemetry collectors
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools for a single customer): same as above but isolated tenancy — included?
- Private (VPC / private deployment): control plane still Redwood-managed but data plane runs in customer VPC — what is in-scope for your engagement?
- On-prem: fully customer-managed appliances — included only if Acme requests Redwood assistance?

Other specific questions: are ephemeral support tunnels / jump hosts used for incident response considered in-scope? Do we have permission to test internal operator consoles and any attendant SSO integrations?

We attached our standard questionnaire (bh_standard_questionnaire.pdf) and proposed baseline tests. Please confirm scope so we can map assets and produce a final plan.

Thanks,
Ben Hargreaves
Blue Harbor Security
sec+bh@blueharbor.com

---
(attachment: bh_standard_questionnaire.pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: sec+bh@blueharbor.com
Cc: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming vulnerability assessment — scope confirmation

Hi Ben / Alex,

Thanks — appreciate the checklist. High level position from Redwood for this engagement (so we can align Acme expectations):

1) Hosted (Redwood-managed): IN SCOPE. That includes Redwood control plane APIs, management consoles exposed to customers, our hosted runtime nodes (where model inference runs), and any telemetry collectors in our managed environment.

2) Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated capacity): IN SCOPE. Dedicated GPU pools that Redwood operates on behalf of Acme are covered — they are Redwood infrastructure even if committed to one customer.

3) Private (VPC): MIXED SCOPE. There are two Private variants we use: 
   - Private (Redwood control plane + customer VPC data plane): IN SCOPE for Redwood-managed control plane components (APIs, orchestration, connectors) and Redwood agents that we deploy into the customer VPC when those agents run as part of Redwood's managed feature set. Customer-owned VPC resources (customer-managed subnets, customer-managed compute, on-prem storage) are OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood's deliverables unless explicit access/consent is provided by Acme and a separate scoping addendum is signed.
   - Private (fully on-prem package where the customer runs both control plane and data plane): OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood. Redwood will provide guidance and an inventory of components that we ship, but the customer must arrange testing for their own environment.

4) On-prem appliances: OUT OF SCOPE unless contractually included.

5) Support tunnels / ephemeral bastions: IN SCOPE only if they are part of the production path or used for automated operator actions against production systems. Ad-hoc break-glass tunnels initiated only during incident response are out-of-scope unless Acme confirms otherwise.

6) SSO / IdP integrations: IN SCOPE for Redwood-managed endpoints and redirect handlers; the customer side of the IdP and their assertion endpoints are out-of-scope.

Next steps we propose:
- Blue Harbor to produce an asset list mapping to the categories above.
- Redwood (Karthik/Rishi) will provide the latest rdw_infrastructure_scope_v2.pdf and a short support_tunnel_diagram.png to show where tunnels exist and who controls them.
- Target: finalize scope by Oct 7 so testing can start week of Oct 11.

Karthik / Rishi: can you attach the two artifacts and confirm the ETA for logs/access we will grant to Blue Harbor (read-only telemetry, jump-host accounts, etc.)?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

From: Blue Harbor Security <sec+bh@blueharbor.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming vulnerability assessment — scope confirmation

Naomi — thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple quick follow-ups from our asset-mapping team: 

- For the Private (Redwood control plane + customer VPC) variant, can you confirm whether KV cache endpoints and model artifacts ever persist outside the customer VPC (e.g., backups or cold storage in Redwood-managed buckets)? If so, those storage paths would need testing.

- For Dedicated pools, do operator-level consoles share the same SSO tenant as Hosted customers, or are they isolated? We need to know for credentialed testing.

- For ephemeral support tunnels: will Redwood provide immutable audit logs and links to session recordings for test validation?

We can proceed with the draft plan once those three items are clarified.

Best,
Ben
Blue Harbor

---
(attachment: bh_followup_matrix.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: sec+bh@blueharbor.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming vulnerability assessment — scope confirmation

Hi Ben, Naomi,

Quick answers from infra: 

- KV cache & model artifacts: Redwood does not persist customer model weights or full KV caches in Redwood-managed long-term buckets for Private (VPC) deployments. For Hosted and Dedicated, artifacts and caches may be stored in encrypted Redwood-managed object storage for short retention windows (metrics, cold cache dumps) — these storage paths are IN SCOPE for Hosted/Dedicated tests. We will provide exact bucket names in the asset list.

- Operator consoles for Dedicated: we run a dedicated SSO tenant per customer for Dedicated capacity in most cases; however, some legacy Dedicated customers still share a managed SSO shard. For Acme's Dedicated instance we have a dedicated tenant (isolated) — credentialed tests will target a customer-specific tenant.

- Support tunnels / audit logs: we will provide session audit logs and recordings where available; the default retention is 90 days. We will supply read-only links and a short manifest (see support_tunnel_diagram.png) to Blue Harbor prior to testing.

Rishi — we'll need to coordinate minimal privilege jump-host accounts and timestamped audit exports. Can you prepare the access bundle by EOD Oct 7?

Laura — looping in Product (for any policy exceptions) in case Acme requests Redwood to include customer-managed VPC endpoints under our scope — that will need a contractual addendum.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
